speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome. I see you have sudden onset abdominal pain; to help me understand the cause, could you tell me exactly where the pain is located and if it is sharp or dull? Also, have you experienced nausea, vomiting, or fever since the pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your recent myocardial infarction and the bloody stools, have you noticed any changes in your bowel movements, such as difficulty passing gas or a sense of rectal fullness? Also, do you have a history of diverticulosis or diverticulitis?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe abdominal pain. I also have Bloody loose bowel movements, No vomiting, Sudden onset. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Migraine and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The previous physician's suggestion of migraine is highly unlikely given your age, sudden abdominal pain, and bloody stools; instead, could you tell me if the pain has moved from your belly button to your lower right side, or if you have noticed a hard, tender lump in that area?
